title: Credit Card Web Portal Redesign · First PREMIER Bank
jpTitle: クレジットカード Webポータル リデザイン
summary: Led a discovery audit of First PREMIER Bank's credit card portal that found the root cause was a total absence of design infrastructure, not cosmetic issues. Prioritized 4 of 10 flows for rebuild — account setup, login, summary, payments — and built a 125+ component design system in three layers, later adopted org-wide, including by the mobile app team's 2022 v2.0.

angles.product: The audit's finding wasn't a list of broken screens — it was that there was no shared component layer at all, so any fix would regress. The two-part response — rebuild four priority flows, then build the 125+ component system underneath — addressed both the symptom and the cause.
angles.business: A design system built for one bank portal was later adopted by an unrelated team (mobile app v2.0) and then became the org-wide standard — evidence the underlying architecture, not just the four rebuilt flows, was the actual deliverable.

mine: Led the discovery audit to find the structural root cause rather than catalog every individual problem
Identified that the portal's issues stemmed from a complete absence of design infrastructure, not cosmetic problems
Set the two-level fix: rebuild the critical flows for immediate impact, and build a system to prevent recurrence
Prioritized 4 of 10 flows by frequency times pain severity — account setup, login, summary, payments
Led design direction, system architecture and screen delivery across the full engagement
Built the design system in three layers: foundation tokens, components, and patterns
team: Not separated on the source page — team scope to be confirmed. Concentrix Catalyst is credited as the bank's design partner engagement.

metrics.label: design system became the org-wide standard by 2023, including the mobile app team's 2022 v2.0 release
metrics.basis: as reported on the case-study page

narrative.problem: The portal had been built incrementally over years: the same account information appeared in multiple places with different interaction patterns, users couldn't complete basic tasks like making a payment without redundant screens, and service call volume was climbing because users couldn't self-serve.
built: Rebuilt account setup, login, summary and payments flows
125+ component design system in 3 layers: Foundation, Components, Patterns

business: Service calls decreased in 2022 as streamlined payment and account flows removed friction
The mobile app team adopted the same system for their 2022 v2.0 release
The system became the org-wide design standard by 2023+
